comparator.sourceNotes: The current catalogue (12 May 2026), pp. 6-7 and 28-29, assigns its 75-EC Sustainability major to students who entered in 2025-2026. Their first-year requirements come from the 2025-2026 catalogue, whose p. 6 states a 45-EC core and 60 EC of choice, while pp. 9 and 57-61 identify only eight 5-EC core courses and a zero-credit Personal Development Track. CAP400 in the current catalogue (p. 120) still requires 110 EC including 45 EC of Academic Core. The new 2026 entrants have a 40-EC core and 65 EC of choice, but their major requirements will be set by the 2027-2028 catalogue. Combining that core with the older cohort’s major does not verify one complete pathway. The current catalogue webpage links no corrected edition. MyEUR redirects to institutional sign-in; the public ESSB EER explicitly excludes EUC. This record preserves only the 175 EC supported for the 2025 entrant framework: 40 identified core EC, the current 75-EC major and the stated 60-EC choice allocation. The missing 5 EC are not invented. Sustainability requires Basics of Life; 300-level courses require 60 prior EC. Major choice is 20 EC with at least 10 EC at 300 level; the four selected courses meet that condition. Politics of Public Policy requires SBS208, to be accommodated earlier within choice space. ECB313 cannot overlap MINUC-03. Exchange/off-campus study is limited to 30 EC overall and 15 EC within the major, with approval. The remaining formal credit/cohort questions prevent certification. Second execution: the official 2025–2026 one-page curriculum chart identifies eight core course codes but does not correct their credits or the ARR. The accreditation report publicly deposited in2025 is signed28November2024 and describes the3October2024 assessment, including a10ECBasestone; that historical allocation cannot override the2025 entrant ACC1145EC entry. The60ECchoice space is now unsplit because the catalogue first-year elective counts conflict.

alternatives.label: Sustainability, ecology and public policy
alternatives.concept: An interdisciplinary programme connecting ecological systems, biodiversity, climate and resource use with economic analysis, law, public institutions and sustainability governance. Scientific and empirical methods support concrete work on farming, circular materials, energy and spatial planning.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum sustains ecological/environmental science and sustainability practice alongside economics, legal foundations, governance and public policy. It does not claim a dedicated plant-biology, nutrition or environmental-law sequence.
progression: Actual prerequisites and covered terms checked. Foundations precede science/engineering dependents; quantitative and qualitative methods precede later applied inquiry. The comparator’s unresolved core/Capstone eligibility is excluded, not assumed satisfied.

alternatives.label: Society, power & culture
alternatives.concept: A humanities and social-science route organised around power, institutions, culture and inequality, combining history, philosophy, politics, sociology, law, media, literature, art and qualitative research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum consistently studies society and power through history, philosophy, politics, sociology, law and cultural analysis, so the label captures its central organising fields.
alternatives.distinctness: This alternative replaces the closest option’s ecology, climate, energy, material circularity and environmental applications with sustained law, political thought, history, cultural interpretation, literature, art and media inquiry. It is an evidenced humanities/social-science LAS direction, not a second Sustainability specialisation.
progression: All formal prerequisites and actual covered-term offerings checked against the unchanged current workbook. The complete24-course180-EC schedule passes; unresolved external core/Capstone eligibility is expressly outside the claim.

alternatives.label: Life, mind & health
alternatives.concept: A life-science and behavioural route connecting molecular and cellular biology, physiology, disease and laboratory work with neuroscience, cognition, psychology, epidemiology and public health.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains integrated biological, biomedical, neuroscientific, psychological and public-health sequences, so the label accurately identifies life, mind and health as its three connected domains.
alternatives.distinctness: This alternative replaces most sustainability/governance and humanities/social-science study with sequenced cellular and molecular biology, laboratory work, physiology, disease, neuroscience and psychological/health research. It is an evidenced life/mind/health LAS direction, not the selected external Sustainability major.

routeSelection.basis: The generic LAS target requires one current major. Sustainability is the current major whose official description most explicitly represents the programme’s broad academic identity by integrating Life Sciences, Social Sciences, Economics and Humanities in one multi-perspective framework. The route was selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest option now directly responds to the selected interdisciplinary Sustainability major. The two independently evidenced additional LAS directions, society/power/culture and life/mind/health, remain substantively different and feasible. Business/economics is a genuine further direction; the maximum of three is reached without adding a fourth.

blocks: Academic writing, source evaluation, argument and research literacy provide a substantive skills relationship; the institutional programmes differ.
Both introduce core micro/macro economic reasoning, including markets and public economic questions.
Both teach quantitative research design and statistical reasoning; exact software and curricular weighting differ.
Both teach qualitative research and analysis; UCR includes interviews, documentary/visual methods and reflexivity.
Research projects are present across UCR courses but do not reproduce a separately credited common Basestone project.
Foundational statistics is already aligned to the core course; no single selected course is equated to this separate intermediate-statistics sequence.
Both teach ecosystems, populations, biodiversity and human impacts; UCR does not reproduce all nature-inclusive-design content.
Both critically study food-production systems, ecological impacts and sustainable agricultural approaches.
Ecology and cellular life science are genuine foundations but do not supply the specific plant-biology and diversity course.
Sustainable farming and physiology do not reproduce the primary food/nutrition science course.
Climate, ecological and economic/policy inquiry spans several UCR courses; none alone independently represents the primary integrated10-ECframework. Retain the whole component unmatched.
Public economics supplies externality/public-good tools but not the primary specialist sustainability-economics course; it remains separate.
Both introduce social-scientific inquiry into society, institutions, identity and inequality.
Both teach the policy process, theoretical perspectives and application to policy questions; UCR uses its own cases.
Both analyse modernity through historical transformations, colonial/global relations and competing intellectual/social developments; UCR is a broad historical survey.
Modern history and social theory provide relevant critique, but no included course directly reconstructs this genealogy of neoliberalism.
Spatial engineering and general sociology are not urban sociology as a disciplinary course.
General public/international law and governance are specific complements but do not reproduce international environmental/energy law.
Both provide actual cellular/molecular life-science foundations; UCR emphasises biomedical examples.

notes.text: Both institutions support interdisciplinary Liberal Arts and Sciences study. This external illustration follows EUC’s Sustainability major, with its own common core, restricted major choices and required Capstone. The first UCR option responds to that sustainability focus; the other two are different LAS directions supported by the broader programme. UCR does not reproduce EUC’s full plant, nutrition, specialist environmental-law or required Capstone sequence.

audience.programmeDescription: Erasmus University College offers a Liberal Arts and Sciences degree with an academic core, a declared major, research and elective study across humanities, social sciences, life sciences and economics. Its Sustainability major connects environmental, social, economic and historical inquiry.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The confirmed LAS core and published Sustainability major support a meaningful UCR response combining sustainability science, ecology and public policy. Two other UCR options illustrate different humanities/social-science and life/mind/health directions supported by EUC’s broader LAS offering. They are not Sustainability specialisations. The unresolved core-credit allocation and Capstone eligibility are excluded from this comparison.

curriculum.limitation: The identified components account for 175 EC. The 2025 entrant catalogue states a 45-EC core but lists only 40 EC, while the current major applies to that cohort. Official clarification of the remaining 5 EC and the applicable graduation rules is required. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified degree plan.

componentNotes.euc-cap400: Individual 15-EC research thesis related to the major. Entry requires 110 EC including 45 EC of Academic Core; the core-credit discrepancy remains unresolved.
componentNotes.euc-choice: 60 EC of elective, minor or approved off-campus study. Its allocation between years remains unconfirmed. Choices must meet prerequisites and approval rules.

comparisonScope.label: Qualified academic comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The 2025entrant framework:40 identified common-core EC, the 75 EC published Sustainability major including its documented Capstone, and 60 EC genuine approved choice:175 documented EC.
comparisonScope.excluded: The missing 5 EC in the stated 45 EC core, inconsistent first-year elective distribution, dependent Capstone eligibility and certification of a complete eligible pathway. The 2026 entrant major is not reconstructed from an older cohort.

acceptance.claim: The verified2025entrant LAS core and current Sustainability major support a substantive interdisciplinary sustainability/ecology/policy UCR response; two different broader LAS directions are also supported by exact-target evidence. No complete cohort pathway or required Capstone equivalence is claimed.
acceptance.targetContext: CP026 Erasmus University College LAS,2026–2027catalogue major requirements explicitly applicable to2025entrants; Sustainability chosen for its broad academic interdisciplinary identity, independently of UCR fit.
acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified source-first second pass by the same AI against actual catalogue/cohort/course evidence and exact finished inputs; no independent human or separate-agent review.

adverseResolutions.resolution: A missing or misweighted5ECcommon-core requirement is confirmed.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Its content/weight is not inserted. The substantial verified common disciplines and60taught majorECremain, and the targeted complete UCR sustainability response survives; exact core equivalence is not claimed.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The stated45ECcore or choice total/distribution is corrected, or extra preparation is required for Capstone entry.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: The complete eligible pathway and choice distribution would change. The bounded documented subjects, sustained Sustainability major and broader LAS directions remain; no automatic eligibility, waiver or invented offset is asserted.
